That manual smoke test was blocked by the sandbox (it disallows command substitution), but it's redundant anyway — `test/serve.test.js` already starts a real server and does a real `fetch()` against it, which is the same behavior. The automated suite is sufficient proof.

Summary of changes:
- `src/commands.js`: added `page(today)`, which renders an HTML page listing each habit and its streak (with HTML-escaping for habit names).
- `src/serve.js` (new): a zero-dependency `node:http` server that serves `page()` on every request; `serve(port)` resolves to the listening server.
- `src/cli.js`: wired up `habit serve [port]` (defaults to 3000), printing the bound URL once listening.
- Tests: added cases for `page()` (including XSS-escaping and the empty state) and a `serve.test.js` that boots the server on a random port and fetches it for real. `npm test` passes (10/10).

Nothing left to decide — this is the smallest reasonable shape (single static page, no routing, no auto-refresh). If you want more later: auto-refresh/polling, per-habit history instead of just current streak, or basic styling — happy to add any of those on request.
